title: Launch Window Latency Hedging and API Backpressure Coordination
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: define and deliver a cross-surface mechanism to hedge launch-window latency spikes by coordinating API-level backpressure, runtime admission controls, and Console visibility. This ticket covers the PM-level orchestration: spec the API backpressure signals, prioritize runtime admission changes, create console dashboards/alerts, and author the launch runbook for coordinated cutover and rollback. The aim is to reduce outage surface during high-concurrency launches and model rollouts while preserving critical SLOs for premium customers.
decisions: Standardize a lightweight backpressure header and 429 semantics exposed by runtime and gateways
Primary hedging lever will be token-based admission throttles with region-aware thresholds
Canary gating will be done by region + route; console shows gating and allows manual override
Opted against synchronous client-side retry suppression in this phase to minimize SDK churn; will iterate in SDK-2
acceptance_criteria: Backpressure header spec accepted by eng/console teams and versioned in API guide
Runtime implements admission throttle and exposes metrics for per-route hedging
Console dashboard shows hedging state, per-route token burn, and automated gating signals
End-to-end canary (shadow traffic -> controlled ramp -> gating) executed with <5% error delta vs baseline
Runbook and rollback checklist published and rehearsed in launch rehearsal
tasks: PM: finalize spec and stakeholder signoff (Confluence link)
ENG: implement backpressure header and admission control in runtime (ENG-35100)
SRE: add synthetic canary and Datadog dashboard panels
Console: add UI for gating state, manual override and per-route telemetry
DX: publish SDK guidance for handling new 429/backpressure signals (docs + code samples)
QA: create end-to-end test harness for canary scenarios
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive throttling reduces latency but increases client-side retries; we chose token admission to allow smoother degradation
Alternative considered: central rate-limiter service; rejected for first iteration due to operational blast radius
This approach is intentionally incremental: signal + runtime gating + visibility. SDK changes deferred to avoid breaking GA clients
We will monitor 95/99th latencies and token-burn ratios during the first two weeks post-rollout

2025-01-24 - SRE prototyped canary job; early metrics show heat for high-token paths in region-us-west-2.
2025-01-31 - Design review: Console team proposed compact gating UI to reduce cognitive load; accepted pending microcopy updates.
2025-02-07 - Implementation in progress: runtime PR opened and internal integration tests passing in CI; manual canary scheduled week of 2025-02-18.
risk_mitigation: Pre-launch: run three synthetic canaries with varying sequence lengths to validate thresholds
During launch: enable automated slow-roll gates tied to Datadog alerts to avoid manual error-prone decisions
Post-launch: 72-hour high-touch rota with on-call SRE + runtime engineer and PM observability checks
Fallback: ability to disable hedging per-region per-route via console and return to previous runtime configuration
